Two centred Greek inscription blocks in the middle of the page, each in capitals with lines set short. A short English caption ("Alter Lapis Athenis in Gymnasio.") between the first and second inscription. The third inscription is broken off at the foot. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword.

main_text.p: adultum diebus illis festis in palaestram. Magistratus autem hic, cuius curae erant commissa τὰ διδασκαλεῖα [?] καὶ τὰ γυμνάσια [?], dictus est Κοσμητὴς, de quo vetus Lapis Athenis in Gymnasio.

Qui Gymnasiarcha simpliciter dicitur, τῷ παίδων [?] intelligitur, Magistratus Κοσμητὴς nomen additur, quia curae gymnasiorum erat praefectus. Habebant quoque Ephebi sua gymnasia, & suum Κοσμητὴν [?], de quo Erotianus in Lexico Hippocratis: κόσμου [?], τάξεως [?]. ἁρμονία [?] δὲ ἡ ἐν λέξει [?]. καὶ γὰρ κοσμίους λέγεσθαι τοὺς διὰ ἐξεῖς [?], καὶ Κοσμητὰς [?], τοὺς τῶν Ἐφήβων ὑπαξίας [?] παιδοτρόφους [?]. Sed in his Gymnasiis non eadem habebant μαθηταὶ [?] Ephebi, quas pueri in suis: iam enim sollertes erant in literis, in palaestra, in musicis, ut de Chaerea Ephebo dixit Terentianus Parmeno: neque haec addiscere illis amplius per oclum licebat: nam tunc toto ἐφηβείας [?] suae tempore [?] ἐπεισοδῶ [?] οἱ Ἐφηβοὶ πάνυ χρῶνται [?] ἐπιφυλάττοντες, ὥσπερ ἤδη μαθηταὶ τῶν [?] γραμματικῶν [?]. Quare etiam eorum μαθηταὶ erant γραμματικοὶ in Gymnasiis; unde auctor Axiochi scribit: ἐπειδὴ δὲ εἰς τοὺς Ἐφήβους ἐἰσγάφη [?], καὶ φόβος χείρων εἴη [?], καὶ Λύκειον [?], καὶ Γυμναστιαρχία [?]. Meminit Λυκείου, quia ibi ficiebant μαθηταὶ γραμματικοί. Interpres Comici ad Pacem: Λύκειον δὲ Γυμνάσιον Ἀθήνησιν, ὅπου παρὰ τὸ πολέμου ἐδόκουν γυμνάζεσθαι. Huius Gymnasiarchae Ephebo-rum, & Cosmetae mentio in veteri Lapide Venetiis olim è Græcia adducto.

page.notes: The Greek is small and partly broken; words marked [?] are uncertain, and the Greek of the Erotianus and Axiochus passages is only approximate. The first Greek line of the first inscription and the accents on the capital Greek are not clear. The third inscription is cut off at the foot of the page. The ΦΛ in the second inscription is as printed. No marginal notes, footnotes or catchword are visible.
